review: 1:1 צֶלֶם עַצְמוּתוֹ — Hebrews 1:3 (אֲשֶׁר הוּא זֹהַר כְּבוֹדוֹ וְצֶלֶם עַצְמוּתוֹ); the Arabic رَسْمَ الْجَوْهَرِ is that verse, and Hebrew keeps both nouns rather than paraphrasing.
2:1 בֶּן־חֵיקוֹ — 'Son of His bosom' (John 1:18, ὁ ὢν εἰς τὸν κόλπον); the Arabic ابْنَ حِضْنِهِ is the same idiom, and חֵיק is the biblical word for the bosom.
2:2 מִי זוּלָתְךָ יַגִּיד — the Arabic مَنْ سِوَاكَ يُخْبِرُ is a rhetorical question; זוּלָתְךָ is the glossary word for 'besides You' and keeps the question sharp.

4:2 אֶחָד בְּעַצְמוּת — 'one in essence', for وَاحِدًا فِي الْجَوْهَرِ; the term is credal rather than biblical, but it is the fixed liturgical rendering and no scriptural phrase carries the doctrine in four syllables.
4:4 שֵׂה אֱלֹהִים הַשָּׁחוּט — 'the slain Lamb of God' (John 1:29, שֵׂה הָאֱלֹהִים); the Arabic حَمَلَ اللهِ الذَّبِيح is that title, and שָׁחוּט is the participle of the sacrificial verb.
5:2 חֲמַת מִשְׁפַּט אֵל — 'the wrath of God's judgment'; the Arabic غَضْبَةَ الْعَدْلِ الْإِلٰهِيّ is a genitive chain, and Hebrew keeps two constructs so the line ends on the adjective.
